title: Annotatio III §.III open: Third Consociation attempt FRANCOFURTANUM — after Luther’s death, Melanchthon still living; Estates and Otto Henry call twenty-five theologians (1557–1558)
pass_a_gloss: §. III. The Third Effort of this, that is of the Reformation Century, is the FRANKFURT one, after the death of Luther, Melanchthon nevertheless still surviving, in the years 1557 and 1558, undertaken by the Imperial Estates themselves and their standard-bearer, Otto Henry the Palatine, twenty-five Theologians having been summoned to Frankfurt, and among these Johann Pistorius, Andreas Hyperius, and Nicolaus Rhodingus, Marburg Professors, commonly held to be rigid Calvinists.
pass_b_english: §. III. The third Consociation attempt of this Reformation century is the Frankfurt one.
It came after Luther’s death, while Melanchthon was still alive — in 1557 and 1558 — undertaken by the Imperial Estates and their leader, Otto Henry the Palatine.
Twenty-five theologians were called to Frankfurt; among them Johann Pistorius, Andreas Hyperius, and Nicolaus Rhodingus, Marburg professors commonly counted as rigid Calvinists.
source_text:
§. III.
Tertium, hujus, i. e. Reformationis Seculi, Molimen, FRANCOFURTANUM est, post fata Lutheri, Melanchthone tamen adhuc superstite, annis 1557. & 1558., ab ipsis Imperii Statibus & horum Antefignano, Ottone Henrico Palatino, susceptum, evocatis Francofurtum, 25. Theologis, hosque inter Joh. Pistorio, Andrea Hypperio, & Nicolao Rhodingo, Professoribus Marpurgensibus, rigidis vulgò habitis Calvinistis.
